## What This Is

**If you installed any version, apply this update.** Through v3.15.0 the Permanent Floor gate refused a shell delete only when the command named a protected file by extension. A directory, a `.json`, an image or a glob inside your vault walked through.

The gate leads. Behind it, seventeen skills receive the rules their canonical versions learned since they shipped, two scripts stop stamping tomorrow's date in the evening, two model slugs that left their catalogs are marked, and the file that states this repo's version is now checked against the changelog on every push.

## The Defect

`pre-tool-approval-gate.sh` protects files whose extension is in `PROTECTED_EXTENSIONS`, which ships as `md`. Fired at a fresh v3.15.0 clone with `SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT` unset, it returned these exits (2 refuses, 0 allows):

```
exit 2  rm "Library/North Star.md"
exit 0  rm -rf "Council Chamber/Pending Plans/Support Files/Old Run"
exit 0  rm "Council Chamber/scripts/package.json"
exit 0  git rm -r "Inbox/old exports"
exit 0  rmdir Scriptorium/empty
exit 0  node -e "require('fs').rmSync('Scriptorium/card.png')"
exit 0  find "Inbox/tmp" -name "*.json" -delete
exit 0  git clean -fd Library
```

One refusal in eight. A directory wipe never names a `.md`, so the gate never saw one. The upstream vault found and closed the same hole in its own copy on 2026-10-09, and its descendants stayed open until this release.

## The Fix

**The rule.** A delete whose target resolves inside one of the vault's top-level containers is refused whatever the extension, including a directory and the vault root itself. The shell gate keeps its extension rules for single files and gains a container rule in front of them.

**The configuration.** A `CONTAINERS` line sits beside `PROTECTED_EXTENSIONS` in the gate, pipe separated, spelled as the folder names: `Council Chamber|Library|Vault (Archive)|Inbox|Scriptorium|Explorations`. Add your own top-level folders there.

**The reading.** `container-delete.mjs` reads the payload (quotes, heredocs, nested `bash -c`, `cd` moving the working directory, interpreter deletes in node and python, PowerShell `Remove-Item`, `cmd /c rmdir` and `del`, `git rm`, `git clean`, `find -delete`, `unlink`, `shred`) and prints `BLOCK: <reason>` or nothing. The shell gate refuses on `BLOCK`.

**The walls.** Allowed: `node_modules` anywhere, `.runtime/`, a search or print that only mentions a delete verb (`grep -n del`, `rg rmtree`, `sed -n '/rmSync/p'`), a commit message or echo text that names a delete, a dry run (`git clean -nd`), a delete outside the vault, a path built at run time, and the same container names in a different repo when the session's working directory sits outside the vault.

**Fails closed.** If the module is missing or exits nonzero there is no verdict, and the gate refuses the call with `FLOOR GATE INERT` on stderr. A Floor guard resolves no verdict toward refusal. This matches the Node paragraph in the README: the guards refuse shell commands when they cannot reach Node.

**Known limits, named so nobody reads silence as coverage:** a path built at run time, a delete fed through a pipe (`xargs rm`, `Get-ChildItem | Remove-Item`), a string passed to an interpreter script as an argument, and a file sitting directly in the vault root.

**The test.** `floor-gate-selftest.mjs` gains 59 cases under "Container deletes", every must-refuse shape above and every wall, plus one case that removes the module and confirms even `git status` is refused. Each must-refuse case was watched failing against the v3.15.0 gate before the fix landed. The suite runs 92 cases and passed three consecutive runs with identical counts, then the full CI step list on a clean snapshot with `SOVEREIGN_VAULT_ROOT` unset.

## If You Are Updating an Existing Vault

1. **Apply the three guard files first:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/se-update.mjs" --check` then `--apply` for `pre-tool-approval-gate.sh`, `container-delete.mjs` and `floor-gate-selftest.mjs`. They live under `Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/`.
2. **Edit `CONTAINERS`** in the gate if your vault's top-level folders differ from the shipped six. The names must match your folder names exactly.
3. **Fire the positive control:** `node "Council Chamber/scripts/hooks/floor-gate-selftest.mjs"`. Expect `pass=92 fail=0`. Green means it refused what it must refuse and allowed what it must allow.
4. **Probe your own gate once by hand**, from a script file rather than the command line so your own gate does not refuse the probe: a payload whose command is `rm -rf "Library/anything"` must exit 2, and one whose command is `rm -rf "Council Chamber/scripts/node_modules"` must exit 0.
5. **If your agent has customized the gate**, hand it this spec rather than the diff: a container rule in front of the extension rules, a configurable container list, a module that reads the command and returns `BLOCK` or nothing, refusal on a missing verdict, and the test list in `floor-gate-selftest.mjs` as the acceptance suite. The recipient owns the code. This file owns the standard.

## What Else Changed

**Seventeen skills catch up with their canonical versions.** Each change below is a rule the upstream vault learned in use since the skill shipped. The published copies had kept their version numbers while the rules moved, which is the stale-skill failure this repo's stewardship pass exists to catch.

- **Autonomous Improvement Session.** Every decision and plan entry on the board ends with `Verified: <live check>, <result>`, and the whole board is delivered in the closing message. The hands bucket holds only what the Sovereign alone can physically do. The Floor scope statement now covers the skill's own files and binds shell commands and every file type. A learning loop: a ledger of rulings never re-raised, a scan that cannot catch a planted defect reports "unverified", previous fixes are re-checked at each run start. Reads go through a read-only database connection only. Scans return a count, an instrument and a reason when they did not run. Commit by explicit pathspec only. Research one category per run. A circuit breaker for monitor-filed issues. Model routing cut to five lines. Two gated external-write forms in the External Orientation block.
- **Batch Archival.** The template copy was the oldest of its three homes and is rebuilt from the published form: workflow, status rules, readiness audit, time-gated material, approval and model routing. Status `active`.
- **Brainstorm.** The scrappiest real test ships with its read rule: continue if, rework if, stop if and what result would tell us nothing, written before the test goes live and fired on an event or a count rather than a date.
- **Manuscript Anti-AI Edit Pass.** Grain protection: constructions matching an author's ledger of sanctioned habits pass every sweep.
- **Pending Plan Implementation.** The Software Build Protocol (idempotency check, evidence strategy chosen before the edit, two-hop trace, worker dispatch contract, parallel safety check, commit heuristic, compound before close). Raw pulls kept beside excerpts. An External Orientation block.
- **Playwright.** A direct social-post URL may bounce to a login wall; check the landed URL and try the platform's share or mobile URL.
- **Researcher.** A Verify phase before presenting, a mandatory save path, report-to-file dispatch for long findings, workers that read the open web separated from workers that read private files, and every finding labeled observed, reported, reasoned, felt or unknown with two rival explanations required of any causal claim.
- **Self-Healing.** An External Orientation block: no outward call of its own, external failures return to the Sovereign, external calls never auto-retry.
- **Session Closeout.** The continuation prompt gets a timing test, and on the command surface a finished item leaves rather than being restated in the past tense.
- **Source Harvest.** Tally component licenses, search in your own words, read a mechanism's scope before marking it covered, and check every quote with an instrument carrying a known-present and a known-absent control.

**Ways of Knowing.** The Challenge and Illumination Codex gains Section XII: every claim carries its kind (observed, reported, reasoned, felt, unknown), the kind travels into every summary, and a felt read is neither promoted to observed nor discounted to zero.

**Two model slugs left their catalogs.** `qwen/qwen3-coder:free` is absent from OpenRouter and `meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct` from NVIDIA NIM as of 2026-10-12. The External Model Routing Codex marks both and the example invocation uses a slug present in its catalog. A retired model ID in a template is a broken install, so verify a slug against the live catalog before pinning it.

**Today means the local day.** `backup-vault.mjs` and `decision-journal.mjs` stamped the UTC day, which west of Greenwich reads tomorrow in the evening. Both now import `Council Chamber/scripts/lib/local-date.mjs`.

**Parallel workers write scratch files under their own subfolder.** Engineering Codex, Orchestration Mode. Two workers sharing one scratch root overwrote each other's scripts.

**Frontmatter Obsidian could not read.** Twelve wikilinks in YAML list items across six files were unquoted, which Obsidian's property parser rejects. All twelve are quoted.

**PendingPlan template** gains an `approved-date` field beside `status`.

**AGENTS.md names the current release, and CI checks it.** The version line read v3.11.0 while v3.15.0 was the Release, for four releases, because no check read that line. A new CI step compares it to the newest CHANGELOG heading and fails on a mismatch. It was watched failing on the mismatch before the line was corrected.

## Prerequisites

v3.15.0. Node on PATH, as the README requires.

## Optional?

No. The container rule closes a hole in the Permanent Floor that every installed vault carries.

<!-- Easter egg: the probe that proved this gate open was itself refused, twice, by the gate it was written to test, because a command line that fires a delete looks exactly like a delete. The tester had to become a file before the guard would let it near the guard. A vault is made of folders and a sentence is made of verbs, and both are read by something that cannot tell a mention from an act. That is the whole problem, and it is also the whole protection. -->
